title: ritonavir
summary: Ritonavir (Norvir®) is a protease inhibitor approved in March 1996 for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. Initially approved as a protease inhibitor, the compound’s role as a PK enhancer, increasing systemic longevity of other drugs through its inhibition of the drug-metabolizing enzyme CYP3A4, became a key utility for HIV-1 infection treatment. This PK-boosting ability was called to action again during the COVID-19 pandemic, gaining approval in combination with the SARS-CoV-2-targeting nirmatrelvir as Paxlovid®—making it a compound leveraged in global pandemics for two different diseases.

title: selgantolimod
summary: Gilead’s selgantolimod (GS-9688) is a presystemic, orally dosed, TLR8-selective agonist developed for chronic HBV infection. Optimization improved TLR8 selectivity and limited systemic exposure for a “soft drug” approach to limit broad immune activation. Key to this project was the use of the woodchuck hepatitis virus model, which provided key evidence of durable antiviral activity supporting clinical development. However, limited efficacy in Ph. 2 ultimately led to selgantolimod’s removal from Gilead’s pipeline in 2026.

title: enpatoran (M5049)
summary: Enpatoran (M5049) is a dual TLR7/8 antagonist currently in clinical development for lupus. Lupus erythematosus is a chronic heterogenous autoimmune disease characterized by production of pathogenic autoantibodies, with SLE accounting for ~70% of lupus cases, and can occur with or without skin-specific manifestations known as CLE. In the Ph. 2 WILLOW trial, enpatoran treatment led to significantly reduced disease severity in CLE patients, but not for SLE patients—motivating the initiation of the Ph. 3 ELOWEN trials for enpatoran’s potential regulatory registration in CLE.

These results raise questions about the relationship between tau level reduction and clinical efficacy in AD.

summary: Tango Therapeutics has advanced TNG456, its third oral, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor, into clinical trials. Tango dosed the first patient in a Ph. 1/2 trial in May 2025 and published the molecule’s discovery story in May 2026.

title: golidocitinib (AZD4205 / DZD4205)
summary: Golidocitinib (AZD4205/DZD4205) is an oral, selective JAK1 inhibitor discovered by AstraZeneca and developed by Dizal for oncology. The molecule applies JAK1-selective pathway inhibition to r/r PTCL, aiming to suppress JAK–STAT-driven lymphoma biology while avoiding cytopenias linked to JAK2 inhibition. After receiving FDA Fast Track designation, golidocitinib was conditionally approved in China for r/r PTCL in 2024 based on JACKPOT8 Part B, where it achieved a 44% ORR.

title: IMU-856
summary: IMU-856 is Immunic’s clinical-stage, selective SIRT6 inhibitor for gastrointestinal diseases.
